page: Microsoft Azure D4s_v3 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DSv3 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon E5-2673 v4 processor operating at 2.3 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is limited to a 33 GB temporary disk, though the instance supports Premium Storage for external disk attachments. No GPU accelerators are included.

Benchmark results place the processing and memory performance of this instance mostly in the lower tiers. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU metrics fall into the bottom 25%, while Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores rank in the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth tests show poor performance for small cached blocks and weak performance for larger uncached blocks. However, the PassMark memory score achieves an average rating, placing it in the middle 50% of tested hardware.

Given the dedicated CPU allocation and balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the instance is configured for general-purpose workloads that require stable but non-intensive compute resources. It is suitable for basic web serving, light database operations, and small-scale text or image processing. The hardware profile offers an entry-level dedicated resource tier, making it a qualitative option for workloads where burstable CPU credits are undesirable but high-compute performance is not required.
